question: Which of the following correctly describes the order and primary cellular activity of the first two phases of normal wound healing?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Haemostasis precedes inflammation; the sequence begins with platelet activation and clot formation before leucocytes arrive.

answers.text: Haemostasis (platelet plug) → Inflammation (neutrophils debride; macrophages orchestrate repair)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Haemostasis (platelet plug and clot) is immediate and is followed by the inflammatory phase in which neutrophils arrive first (hours) to debride, then macrophages (days 2–4) to orchestrate subsequent repair.
Proliferation occurs after haemostasis and inflammation, not before haemostasis.
Remodelling is the final phase and occurs months to years after injury; it cannot precede inflammation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the four overlapping phases of wound healing: haemostasis, inflammation, proliferation and remodelling.
Well done. The correct order is haemostasis → inflammation → proliferation → remodelling.
